questions.question: You approach a section of the road where a flagman is displaying the signal shown on the left. Which of the following statements correctly describes your legal obligation?

options.text: You must stop your vehicle, but you may proceed with caution once you can clearly see that the roadway ahead is free of livestock or road works.
You must stop, and you shall remain stationary until the proceed flag signal is explicitly displayed.
You must slow down significantly and stop only if oncoming traffic or crossing animals block your path.
You must stop, but if the flagman lowers the red flag or walks away from the road, you may proceed immediately.

questions.explanation: The flagman's stop signal (red flag held out) means you must stop and stay stopped until the proceed signal is given.

questions.question: A driver loads a vehicle so that the load projects beyond the rear of the vehicle. What is the maximum permitted rear projection before the load becomes illegal?

options.text: 1.25 metres
1.5 metres
1.8 metres
2 metres

questions.explanation: A load may not project more than 1.8 m beyond the rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: You are driving a heavy vehicle down a steep mountain pass and notice the alternating red and white chequered pattern painted on the road surface ahead. Which statement correctly identifies the purpose and legal rule regarding this marking?

options.text: It marks a compulsory stopping zone where all heavy vehicles must pull over to test their brake temperature before proceeding.
It indicates an arrestor bed ahead, which is a dedicated overrun area designed to safely stop runaway vehicles with brake failure.
It indicates a high-friction deceleration zone meant for normal traffic to slow down rapidly before a sharp bend.
It is a decorative warning marking to indicate that a standard runaway escape road is currently closed for maintenance.

questions.explanation: Red and white chequered road markings indicate an arrestor bed (escape road) for runaway vehicles with brake failure.

questions.question: A goods vehicle has a GVM exceeding 10 000 kg. Which statement is correct regarding yellow reflective material?

options.text: It is only required on the rear of the vehicle
It is compulsory on the sides and rear of the vehicle
It is only required if the vehicle operates at night
It is optional if yellow retro-reflectors are fitted

questions.explanation: Goods vehicles with a GVM over 10 000 kg must have yellow retro-reflective material on the sides and rear.

questions.question: You are driving on a single-lane road and encounter the sign shown below. Which statement correctly describes the road condition ahead and your legal driving position?

options.text: An additional lane is opening up immediately on your right, and you must move into it if you wish to maintain your current speed.
The road will soon widen to include an additional lane on the left, and you are legally required to keep to the far-left lane unless you are overtaking.
A sharp off-ramp or exit lane is splitting to the left, which can only be used by heavy slow-moving commercial vehicles.
The road ahead becomes a dual-carriageway motorway, and the left-hand lane is reserved exclusively for traffic entering from an upcoming slipway.

questions.explanation: This sign shows an additional lane being added on the left; keep left unless overtaking.

questions.question: A motor car's interior rear-view mirror is completely obstructed by cargo. Which arrangement is legally acceptable?

options.text: Remove all mirrors because the cargo blocks visibility anyway
Keep only the interior mirror fitted
Fit an additional exterior mirror on the opposite side and omit the interior mirror
Drive only during daylight hours

questions.explanation: If the interior mirror is obstructed, an additional exterior mirror must be fitted on the opposite side (so mirrors are on both sides).

questions.question: You are driving on a road where this sign is displayed. As night falls and darkness sets in, which rule applies to your maximum speed limit if no other speed limit signs are present?

options.text: The limit remains 120 km/h because a daytime limit automatically extends into the night unless a night-time speed sign is explicitly shown.
You may determine your own safe speed based on visibility, as the 120 km/h restriction is legally cancelled after sunset.
The limit reverts to the general speed limit of the specific road type you are on (e.g., 60 km/h in an urban area or 100 km/h on a rural road).
The limit drops by exactly 20 km/h automatically as a standard safety margin required by the National Road Traffic Act.

questions.explanation: A speed limit shown as a daytime limit applies only during the day; at night the general speed limit for that type of road applies unless another sign says otherwise.

questions.question: What is the maximum turning radius permitted for a motor vehicle used on a public road?

options.text: 11.5 metres
12.5 metres
13.1 metres
14.5 metres

questions.explanation: The maximum turning radius of a motor vehicle is 13.1 m.

questions.question: When you encounter a flagman performing the actions illustrated, what is the exact legal requirement dictated to you as a road user?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop and wait for the flagman to drop the red flag entirely before moving forward.
You are being informed that the road works or hazards ahead are officially clear, and you may resume normal driving speeds.
You are required to reduce your speed, proceed slowly, and maintain a high state of alertness for potential hazards.
You must immediately change lanes or pull onto the shoulder of the road to allow oncoming construction vehicles to pass.

questions.explanation: The flagman's slow-down signal means reduce speed, proceed slowly and be alert for hazards.

questions.question: Which statement regarding number plates is correct?

options.text: A motor car only requires a rear number plate
A trailer requires both front and rear number plates
A motorcycle requires a front and rear number plate
A motorcycle requires only a rear number plate

questions.explanation: Motorcycles (and trailers) carry only a rear number plate; motor cars need front and rear plates.
